summary: Support protected rewritten merges in terminal receipt verification

delivery.outcome: Publish new-project 0.20.2 with fail-closed terminal receipt verification for protected GitHub rebase and squash merges.
nonGoals: Do not weaken target-branch reachability or append-only receipt bindings
Do not trust mutable refs, PR prose or an asserted merge method
Do not change the terminal receipt registry schema
Do not rewrite historical ticket status projections or create a release-only ticket

architecture.decision: Retain direct Git ancestry as the primary terminal proof; accept a rebase only when a linear original head series matches the same-length terminal patch series, and accept a squash only when one terminal commit matches the aggregate protected-head patch.
interfaceChanges: terminalOutcomes verification advances from git-ancestry to git-ancestry-or-rewritten-patch-series
dataChanges: New-project release projections advance from 0.20.1 to 0.20.2
architecture.rollback: Before publication, revert the atomic ticket commit; after publication, issue a newer corrective standard without retargeting immutable tags.

validation.evidence: An advanced target plus protected two-commit rebase and squash both resolve, while mismatched and nonlinear patch evidence is rejected without registry mutation.

commands: for test_script in tests/*.test.sh; do bash "$test_script"; done
validation.evidence: Complete deterministic suite and exact-head governance pass.
